implementation_notes: POSIX gives only the lock primitive, so the structure is built by hand: choose a stripe count N, allocate N pthread_mutex_t values (statically with PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER or at startup with pthread_mutex_init), and map each key through a stable hash (FNV-1a, siphash) reduced modulo N. Each operation locks only its stripe, so unrelated keys proceed in parallel while lock memory stays O(N). pthread_rwlock_t per stripe is the reader-writer variant, and C11 threads offer mtx_t as a portable alternative to pthreads. Prefer the platform's concurrent container when the state is a plain map.
pitfalls: The stripe array must be initialized before any thread can use it; copying an initialized mutex is undefined, so keep the array in one place and pass a pointer to the owner.

Acquiring several stripes for one operation needs a global order (for example ascending stripe index) plus de-duplication when two keys collide onto one mutex: relocking a non-recursive mutex deadlocks.
Without padding or separate allocation, adjacent mutexes share cache lines and contention shows up as cache-line ping-pong rather than lock contention.
